idea-plugin.name: Live SQLite for Android
idea-plugin.description:
Browse and edit the SQLite databases of your Android debug app while it runs, in a tool window.

I built it to add what Android Studio's Database Inspector is missing, starting with a filter for every column.

  • Filter box under every column: plain text, or a comparison like >100 or !=draft.
  • Sort by any column. Filters and sorting apply to the whole table, not only the loaded rows.
  • Rows load 500 at a time, so large tables open fast.
  • Click a foreign key to open the rows it references.
  • Edit cells, set them to NULL, add and delete rows.
  • Run your own SQL, with completion of table and column names, recent queries and favorites per database.
  • Tables from several databases open side by side in tabs, and the plugin reconnects to the same app next time.

Setup

Your app needs the Android-Debug-Database (debug-db) library; the plugin talks to its server inside the app through adb forward. Add JitPack to settings.gradle.kts:

dependencyResolutionManagement {
    repositories {
        maven { setUrl("https://jitpack.io") }
    }
}

and debug-db to the app module's build.gradle.kts:

debugImplementation("com.github.amitshekhariitbhu.Android-Debug-Database:debug-db:1.0.7")

debugImplementation keeps it out of your release build. Then run the app, open the SQLite Browser tool window and press Connect. More in the README.

Screens that read through Room (Flow, LiveData) don't see your edits until they query the database again.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.2.0: a tidier tool window. Tables and query results get a toolbar with a pager, tabs are editor tabs with a close button, filter fields line up with their columns, and the primary key and sort show as header icons. The SQL editor has line numbers, and saved queries fold like a tree.

0.1.0: first release. Browse tables with paging, sorting and a filter per column, follow foreign keys, edit cells and rows, and run your own SQL with completion, recent queries and favorites.
